p: Woodside Leisure Park sits on the north side of Watford, out towards Garston, and it's a proper leisure hub with bowling, cinema and places to eat all in one spot. That makes it easy to build a whole evening around your Gamebox session without having to jump in the car again. Book the game first, then plan food and a few frames around it.

A few pointers to help your team win. Wear trainers and comfortable clothes, and leave coats and bags somewhere safe. Listen properly to the briefing, then split jobs: one person on targets, one on puzzles, one watching the clock. Sessions run for a set time and the game line-up rotates, so choose something that suits your group. Families with younger kids might want a gentler theme, while teens and adults can go for something more intense.

If you're making a day of it, the Warner Bros. Studio Tour London, where you can see sets and props from the Harry Potter films, is at Leavesden on the edge of Watford. It's a big attraction and needs booking well in advance, but it pairs brilliantly with a fun evening out.

In the town centre, the Atria Watford shopping centre is the main place for shops and food, and the Watford Palace Theatre puts on plays and pantos. With Cassiobury Park, the canal and all this on the doorstep, there's no shortage of ways to fill a weekend.
